title: Conclusion of Shahrazad and Shahryar (Português)

full_text:
When the thousand and first night had drawn to its close, Shahrazad concluded her final tale, fell silent, and bowed her head before King Shahryar.

The king looked upon her with luminous eyes overflowing with tears of deep tenderness, respect, and profound gratitude.

Shahrazad called for her attendants, who brought forth three young princes whom she had borne to the king during those three years of storytelling: the first was walking, the second crawled upon the carpet, and the third was a babe in arms.

Shahrazad wept and said: 'O King of the Age! These are your sons. For a thousand and one nights I have unfolded before you the chronicles of ancient kings, the wonders of the seas, the wit of the humble, and the justice of the wise, seeking only to heal your heart from sorrow. If your soul is still troubled by suspicion, I submit to your royal decree; but if my tales have brought light to your mind, grant me life for the sake of these innocent children!'

King Shahryar sprang from his golden throne, lifted Shahrazad in his arms, and wept with heartfelt joy:

'By the Creator of all the heavens, O Shahrazad! My heart was healed long before these children appeared! Your wisdom, patience, and pure virtue have delivered my soul from the darkness of melancholy and saved the daughters of my empire! You are my Queen, my teacher, and the light of my life forever.'

The king summoned his grand vizier—Shahrazad’s father—and embraced him with royal honors. He sent for his brother Shahzaman, who wed Shahrazad’s sister Dunyazad in a magnificent double celebration.

The city of Baghdad was illuminated for thirty days with lanterns and fountains of rosewater; the prisons were opened, debts were canceled, and granaries distributed to the poor. The scribes transcribed all the thousand and one tales in golden letters, preserving them for all generations as an eternal monument to the triumph of wisdom, love, and narrative truth.
moral: The healing power of wisdom, literature, and patience cures the wounded heart and restores peace to an empire. [PT]
